Action Plan:
1. Arrange same-day in-person review at central London clinic for full physical examination of current febrile illness.  
2. Following examination, perform blood work: thick & thin blood films for malaria, full blood count, inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP/ESR) and any additional tests the examining GP deems necessary.  
3. If clinic attendance is not feasible, patient to attend nearest Emergency Department with clinician’s typed note requesting the above investigations.  
4. Advise patient to remain off work until cause of fever identified and clinically fit to return. Medical certificate to be issued after assessment if required.  
5. Administrative staff to telephone patient with appointment details; patient to call the provided number within a few minutes to confirm booking.  
6. Continue symptomatic relief with paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented). Seek urgent care if symptoms worsen (rigors, shortness of breath, confusion).  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Persistent fever with alternating chills and sweats × 7 days.  
• Associated symptoms: Generalized myalgia, marked fatigue, nausea with reduced oral intake, nocturnal sweating. No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, urinary symptoms, neck stiffness, new headache, rash, or joint swelling.  
• Travel history: Returned from rural Vietnam 4 weeks ago; trekking, cycling, river/ farmland exposure. Took daily malaria prophylaxis (drug unknown, possibly two-drug regimen).  
• Past medical history: Chronic mechanical back pain (under physiotherapy); episodic screen-related headaches/migraines.  
• Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine) – dose/route/frequency not documented; Paracetamol & ibuprofen OTC – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: Pollen (hay fever). No drug allergies reported.  
• Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.  
• Social history: 30-year-old female nurse; non-smoker; moderate alcohol intake; exercises several times per week; vaccinations up to date (including Hep-B).

Objective:
• Telephone consultation – no physical examination or vital signs recorded.  
• Investigations: None performed yet; blood tests planned as per Action Plan.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Febrile illness post-travel (possible malaria / pyrexia of unknown origin):  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Malaria (DDx likelihood: High) vs. other infectious or inflammatory causes.  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Malaria – High (DDx).  
     • Acute systemic viral infection (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) – Medium (DDx).  
     • Dengue/arboviral infection – Medium-Low (DDx).  
     • Enteric (typhoid) fever – Low (DDx).  
     • Tuberculosis, infective endocarditis, lymphoma/leukemia, adult-onset Still’s disease—consider if initial tests negative.  
   – Investigations planned: Thick & thin blood films for malaria; full blood count; inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR); additional tests per examining clinician.  
   – Treatment planned: Symptomatic antipyretics; hold off on antimicrobials until diagnosis clarified. Off-work advice.  
   – Relevant referrals: In-person GP clinic today; alternative ED attendance if unable to reach clinic.

2. Chronic mechanical back pain:  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Mechanical low-back pain.  
   – Differential diagnosis: Not revisited today; symptoms stable.  
   – Investigations planned: None today.  
   – Treatment planned: Continue physiotherapy and posture/strengthening program already in place.  
   – Relevant referrals: None at this consult.

3. Episodic tension/migraine headaches:  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Chronic episodic headaches secondary to screen use and weather changes.  
   – Differential diagnosis: Migraine vs. tension-type headache.  
   – Investigations planned: None today.  
   – Treatment planned: Usual self-management; no new therapy discussed.  
   – Relevant referrals: None.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: Temperature, blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, weight/BMI not recorded; medication doses/routes/frequencies not documented.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; no significant inaudible sections impacting data capture.
